note: Showcase farms for the demo. The farmers are illustrative personas, not real people. Locations were chosen and verified by Claude Code on 2026-11-14 with ESA WorldCover, USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer and NASA MODIS land cover in Google Earth Engine.

farms.name: Tagum City rice farm
farms.persona: Illustrative smallholder rice farmer, Tagum City
farms.place: Barangay Buclad, Tagum City, Davao del Norte (Davao Region)

verification.within_tagum_city: OpenStreetMap reverse geocoding: Purok 2, Buclad, Tagum, Davao del Norte (checked Nov 15, 2026)
verification.note: Tagum City is mostly banana and coconut plantations (tree cover); this was the most cropland-dominated spot found inside the city boundary
verification.satellite_crop_pattern: MODIS NDVI 2001-2026 normal peaks in February (0.71) and August (0.76), two rice crops a year; lowest in December-January and May; looks bare November-January. NASA POWER rain is spread through the year (5-9 mm/day) and SMAP root-zone soil stays moist (0.33-0.37)

farms.story: Two rice crops a year (January-April and June-September) leave the field bare from late September to January, in a wet climate with no real dry season. A short legume such as mungbean or peanut could use that window. La Nina floods and heavy rain are the main weather risk here.

sources.claim: Tagum City is among the Davao del Norte rice areas receiving DA hybrid rice seed for the wet cropping season
sources.title: The Philippine Herald: 3 Davao del Norte towns get PHP23 million hybrid rice seeds (2026)

sources.claim: Davao del Norte rice is grown in a wet season and a dry season (PhilRice survey of farming practices by province)
sources.title: PhilRice Ricelytics: Rice farming practices in Davao del Norte

sources.claim: Carmen, Panabo and Tagum were expected to be among the areas hit hardest by La Nina; farmers were urged to adjust their cropping season
sources.title: Manila Bulletin: Davao del Norte farmers urged to adapt vs natural disasters (2024)

sources.claim: Mungbean was the best upland crop for using residual soil moisture after rice
sources.title: AGRIS (FAO) record of a UP Los Banos study on crops after rice

sources.claim: About 20 tropical cyclones enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility each year; 8-9 cross the country
sources.title: PAGASA: Tropical Cyclone Information

farms.name: Central Iowa corn-soybean farm
farms.persona: Illustrative mechanized corn-soybean farmer, Boone County
farms.place: Rural Boone County, Iowa, west of Ames
farms.story: The classic two-crop rotation, mechanized and rain-fed. Fields sit bare from the October harvest to the May planting, through frost and snowmelt. A cereal rye cover crop could hold the soil over winter. A strong contrast with the Philippines farm.

sources.claim: This field alternated soybean and corn every year 2021-2025 (at least 99.5% of the 250 m circle in the main crop)
sources.title: USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer 2021-2025 (via Google Earth Engine, USDA/NASS/CDL)

sources.claim: Corn and soybean planting runs mid-April to early June (57% of corn and 39% of soybeans planted by May 12, 2024); harvest runs mid-September to November
sources.title: USDA NASS: Iowa Annual Crop Progress 2024

sources.claim: Cereal rye is a recommended cover crop in Iowa corn-soybean rotations, terminated before soybean planting
sources.title: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach: cover crop recipe (cereal rye)
